message.content: {"drafts":[{"title":"Considering Nvidia M60 for LLM Inference: Is Its 8x2GB Memory a Dealbreaker Compared to M40?","body":"I'm looking into budget GPUs for local LLM inference and have the Nvidia M40 and M60 on my radar. The M40 is often the go-to recommendation for low-budget rigs (F1), but the M60, despite theoretically offering almost twice the performance and sometimes costing the same or less (F4, F7), tends to be dismissed because of its 8x2GB memory configuration spread across two GPUs (F2). Given that modern LLM tools like Kobold and Ollama support multi-GPU inference (F3), I'm wondering if that memory split is really a significant bottleneck. Even if some performance gains are lost to PCIe overhead (F5), the M60 might still be a better value. My hope is that with 16GB total, I could run half-decent models at okay speeds (F6). Has anyone had experience or thoughts on whether the M60's memory layout limits practical LLM workloads, or if it's worth grabbing at around $100 for local inference?","fact_refs":["F1","F2","F3","F4","F5","F6","F7"]}]}
